This is an [R Markdown](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com) Notebook. When you execute code within the notebook, the results appear beneath the code. 

Try executing this chunk by clicking the *Run* button within the chunk or by placing your cursor inside it and pressing *Ctrl+Shift+Enter*. 

Click the Run Current Chunk button to install the packages.

```{r}
#AS 3504
#Instructor: Jeffrey Zheng

# List of packages to load
required.packages = c("actuar", "ada", "astsa", "bestglm", "boot", "broom", "car", "caret", "class", "cluster", "coefplot", "corrgram", "corrplot", "cplm", "data.table", "datasets", "devtools", "dslabs", "e1071", "elasticnet", "FNN", "fpp2", "gbm", "GGally", "ggplot2", "ggfortify", "glmnet", "gridExtra", "Hmisc","insuranceData", "ISLR", "lmtest", "magrittr", "MASS", "Metrics", "PerformanceAnalytics", "plotly", "pdp", "pls", "plyr", "pROC", "randomForest", "ranger","rattle", "RcmdrMisc", "RColorBrewer", "readr",  "reshape2", "rpart", "rpart.plot", "rugarch", "statmod", "tidyr", "tidymodels", "tidyverse", "titanic", "tree", "tweedie", "xgboost", "xts", "zoo")

#lapply(required.packages, require, character.only=TRUE) # loads all the listed packages

installed_packages <- required.packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())

if (any(installed_packages == FALSE)) {
  install.packages(required.packages[!installed_packages]) # only install those not yet installed
}

installed.packages() # to see the list of all installed packages

options(defaultPackages=c(getOption("defaultPackages"),"actuar", "ada", "astsa", "bestglm", "boot", "broom", "car", "caret", "class", "cluster", "coefplot", "corrgram", "corrplot", "cplm", "data.table", "datasets", "devtools", "dslabs", "e1071", "elasticnet", "FNN", "fpp2", "gbm", "GGally", "ggplot2", "ggfortify", "glmnet", "gridExtra", "Hmisc","insuranceData", "ISLR", "lmtest", "magrittr","MASS", "Metrics", "PerformanceAnalytics", "plotly", "pdp", "pls", "plyr", "pROC", "randomForest", "ranger","rattle", "RcmdrMisc", "RColorBrewer", "readr",  "reshape2", "rpart", "rpart.plot", "rugarch", "statmod", "tidyr", "tidymodels", "tidyverse", "titanic", "tree", "tweedie", "xgboost", "xts", "zoo")) # may take care of need to do library() every time

#Any packages missing, use install.packages() or uncomment out the last line and run it

#install.packages("actuar", dependencies = TRUE) # installs a specific package

```


R Library Installation debug issues I've seen before:
1. If it asks if you want to compile... with options (Yes/No/Cancel), select No.

2. A restart of R Studio sometimes does miracles for no reason.

3. If it gives you an error of cannot download Libraries and asks you if you want to use a Personal Library, force close out.
Reopen R Studio, but right-click and select "Run as Administrator".
It means somehow R wasn't granted the power to download and install stuff.

4. If you can't install packages like bestglm on a Mac, you might need to install gfortran.
https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/GFortranBinaries#MacOS
